phrases.text: Initiative Measure IP26-645 is about taxes on individual income.
In 2026, the Legislature passed a 9.9 percent tax on yearly income over a million dollars, starting in 2028.
IP26-645 would repeal that tax, and bar state and local taxes on individual income.
The Office of Financial Management estimates the state would lose $11.4 billion in revenue over budget years 2027 to 2031.
The Office says the general fund would have less money for schools, colleges and health care.
The Office also expects state agencies to save about $150 million over the same five years.
Opponents say IP26-645 gives the wealthiest a tax break, and cuts funding for schools, healthcare and childcare.
Supporters say IP26-645 repeals the income tax before it starts, so lawmakers can't expand it to everyone.
A yes vote means the 9.9 percent tax would be repealed.
A no vote means the 9.9 percent tax would not be repealed.
